blocks.content: Covers Assam's major tourist destinations, heritage sites, and pilgrimage centres — practically useful GK that overlaps with Geography, History, and Culture chapters, so treat it as a consolidating revision chapter.

items: Kamakhya Temple (Guwahati) — one of the most significant Shakti Peethas, a major centre of Tantric worship, and host to the annual Ambubachi Mela.

Sivasagar — the former Ahom capital, home to numerous historical monuments including the Rang Ghar (an amphitheatre, sometimes cited as one of the oldest surviving amphitheatres in Asia), Talatal Ghar, and the Sivasagar Sivadol (a major Shiva temple complex) and associated tanks built during Ahom rule.
Majuli — beyond its status as a river island, a major pilgrimage and cultural tourism destination given its concentration of satras (neo-Vaishnavite monasteries).
Hajo — a syncretic pilgrimage town near Guwahati, significant to Hindu, Buddhist, and Muslim traditions alike, home to the Hayagriva Madhava Temple and the Poa Mecca shrine.
Kaziranga National Park — Assam's premier wildlife tourism destination, offering elephant and jeep safaris to view the one-horned rhinoceros and other wildlife.
Manas National Park — combines wildlife tourism with scenic riverine and forest landscapes along the Bhutan border.
Umananda Island — a small river island in the Brahmaputra at Guwahati, sometimes cited as one of the world's smallest inhabited river islands, home to a Shiva temple.
Chandubi Lake — a scenic natural lake formed after an earthquake, near Guwahati, popular for eco-tourism and adventure activities.
Assam State Museum (Guwahati) — houses significant archaeological, epigraphic, and cultural artefacts relevant to the state's history.
Srimanta Sankardev Kalakshetra (Guwahati) — a major cultural complex dedicated to preserving and showcasing Assamese art, culture, and heritage, including museums and performance spaces.

The Bhupen Hazarika Setu — a major bridge over the Lohit River connecting Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, notable as one of India's longest river bridges at the time of its construction, named in honour of the celebrated Assamese cultural icon.
Guwahati's evolving urban infrastructure and periodic new landmark developments are occasionally tested in current-affairs-linked tourism questions.

cells:
Exam Tip

• Sivasagar's Ahom-era monuments (Rang Ghar, Talatal Ghar, Sivadol) are frequently tested as a linked set given their shared historical origin — know each monument's specific distinguishing feature.

• The Bhupen Hazarika Setu's engineering/geographic significance (connecting Assam-Arunachal Pradesh over the Lohit) is a commonly tested modern-infrastructure fact.

• Hajo's syncretic religious significance (Hindu-Buddhist-Muslim shared heritage) is a distinctive, frequently tested fact that sets it apart from other purely Hindu pilgrimage sites.
